<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/types/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via ICryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via ICryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via getKernel (symbol, a field of interface HostCryptoProviderContext), getServices (symbol, a method of interface HostCryptoProviderContext))_
- `content/docs/plugins/anatomy.mdx`  _(via getKernel (symbol, a field of interface HostCryptoProviderContext), getServices (symbol, a method of interface HostCryptoProviderContext))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via ICryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level type), rotateKey (literal, a string literal in CRYPTO_PROVIDER_MEMBERS))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via ICryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via ICryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level type), keyedDigest (literal, a string literal in CRYPTO_PROVIDER_MEMBERS), rotateKey (literal, a string literal in CRYPTO_PROVIDER_MEMBERS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/types/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 47 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **41** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c77dd17f2671f35e8f194ca1e63d8cc75bfb861a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8663b53e486c38706c03591a0241f7b2b747757a` — the merge of head `fbc8206285c9f7877adbe479cd7bb525a603efd3` into base `c77dd17f2671f35e8f194ca1e63d8cc75bfb861a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8663b53e486c38706c03591a0241f7b2b747757a && git checkout 8663b53e486c38706c03591a0241f7b2b747757a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c77dd17f2671f35e8f194ca1e63d8cc75bfb861a fbc8206285c9f7877adbe479cd7bb525a603efd3 && git checkout -B drift-repro c77dd17f2671f35e8f194ca1e63d8cc75bfb861a && git merge --no-ff fbc8206285c9f7877adbe479cd7bb525a603efd3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c77dd17f2671f35e8f194ca1e63d8cc75bfb861a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c77dd17f2671f35e8f194ca1e63d8cc75bfb861a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `2ff85dadc556ebc7e2a8b68ebc051be4ff5d5778`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs` run once on a detached worktree of the head, to answer whether the new test file trips the main gate; it ran the head's own copy of the script, which predates main's source-reach half (acd190b223, #30969), so it answered only the alias half (OK) and not the half CI is red on
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts, packages/types/src/crypto-provider-service.ts, packages/types/src/index.ts, .changeset/30948-host-crypto-provider.md + packages/core/src/kernel.ts (use, bootstrap phases, registerService, context), packages/core/src/kernel-base.ts (trigger propagation), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts (options, start), packages/services/service-settings/src/local-crypto-provider.ts (deferredLocalCryptoProvider, settleKeyFileChannel), packages/core/src/capability-composition.ts (resolveCapabilityArgument), packages/cli/vitest-tiers.ts, scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs (head and main copies), packages/cli/package.json (exports)

Face: the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 30993`: 0 of 5 paths hit the governed register; no `packages/spec/src/**` file; `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` says the paths decide no face and the changeset's `Clause-②:` line decides, so `--face declaration` ⇒ `TIER_DEFAULT`. No ④.

Inputs read: card #30948 body; triage 6686459323; claim 6687208082 and its full re-post 6687449788 (file surface, ⛔ list, premise, `CRYPTO_PROVIDER_SERVICE` in `packages/types`); the card thread's record of the seat's three rulings (constant in `@objectstack/types`; two registrations refused without extending `kernel.ts`; the settings shared-instance stated in the PR body); os-dev report 6689416308; the dispatch order; PR #30993 body and file list; the head's check-runs and the red job's log.

### ① Derived judgments

Scope and claim surface.
- Confirmed: the five changed paths are exactly the claim's surface (serve.ts; its test under `packages/cli/`; the `packages/types` constant and its `index.ts` export; one changeset). No `packages/spec/**`, no stack-config knob, no spec key, `LocalCryptoProvider` untouched, no `ui/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `.claude/**`. The service name does not enter `CoreServiceName`; the registered value's type is the unchanged `ICryptoProvider` contract. In claim.
- Confirmed: `packages/types/src/crypto-provider-service.ts:38` exports `CRYPTO_PROVIDER_SERVICE = 'crypto-provider'`, beside the `DATASOURCE_SECRET_RESOLVER_SERVICE` precedent (`packages/types/src/datasource-secret-resolver.ts:47`); `packages/types/src/index.ts:110` re-exports it. One accepted-set addition on `@objectstack/types`.
- Confirmed: `serve.ts` is not an `exports` entry of `@objectstack/cli` (`packages/cli/package.json` exports `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body` only), so `createHostCryptoProvider`, `HostCryptoProviderRefusal`, `refuseTwoCryptoProviderPlugins`, `HostCryptoProvider`, `HostCryptoProviderSource` are internal, not accepted-set.

The registered provider is read after plugin init and before any secret write.
- Confirmed by `serve.ts:6339-6349`: the host plugin's `init` records a registry reader (`ctx.getServices().get(CRYPTO_PROVIDER_SERVICE)`) and an `initDone` that reads the kernel state live; `resolve()` (`serve.ts:6288-6302`) refuses with `HostCryptoProviderRefusal` while the kernel is `idle`/`initializing` and chooses once, at first use or at the host's `kernel:ready` hook. `packages/core/src/kernel.ts:537,569`: the kernel is `initializing` through Phase 1 and `running` before Phase 2 starts, so "every init has run" is exactly what `initDone` reads. `kernel.ts:326` and `kernel-base.ts:140` both supply `getKernel`; `kernel.ts:306` supplies `hook`; `kernel.ts:319-321` `getServices()` returns a fresh copy each call, so the read is live and identity-stable.
- Confirmed: no `LocalCryptoProvider` is built anywhere in `serve.ts` any more (the test's source pin at `serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts:552`, and `grep` on the head: the only remaining mentions are comments and strings). The fallback is the one deferred instance (`serve.ts:5114-5115`), built only inside `local()` when the registry holds nothing.

One instance to the three consumers.
- Confirmed: the data engine gets `hostCrypto.provider` at `serve.ts:5691` after `confirm()` at `:5690`; the datasource secret binder gets it at `:5380`; the default `SettingsServicePlugin` gets it through its existing `cryptoProvider` option at `:5231-5234`. `resolveCapabilityArgument` returns `undefined` for `settings` (`capability-composition.ts:243`), so the spread yields `{ cryptoProvider }`; `SettingsServicePlugin`'s constructor (`settings-service-plugin.ts:200-214`) spreads opts and applies the same `??` defaults as `new Ctor()`, so nothing else about the default settings service changes. `settings-service-plugin.ts:383` reads `this.opts.cryptoProvider ?? new LocalCryptoProvider()`, so the option is honoured.
- Confirmed: the settings plugin's key-file settlement (`settings-service-plugin.ts:298`, `settleKeyFileChannel`) runs in its `start()` regardless of the option, before any consumer of a kernel decrypts; the deferred local provider reads the env at build time (`local-crypto-provider.ts:1325-1329`), so the no-registration fallback still reads the settled key file.

The deferred-provider path.
- Confirmed: the binder is composed before plugins initialize and holds the host provider, which chooses nothing until Phase 1 ends. A credential bound from a `kernel:ready` hook (the datasource admin's rehydration window) resolves to the registered provider, never the local one (test `serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts:438-460`). A seal or open attempted during init is refused and records nothing (test `:462-489`, both plugin orders). So no write can be sealed by `LocalCryptoProvider` before the swap, and nothing is sealed by a provider the boot has not chosen.
- Confirmed: on main the binder's deferred local provider would have built at any first use, phase regardless; on the branch a use during init refuses. No shipped consumer seals or opens during init (the binder's only holder rehydrates at `kernel:ready`; the settings service seals on `set()`; the engine is wired after start), so this refusal takes nothing away from a consumer that exists today. Noted in ③.

Fallback only when none registered; production refusal unchanged on that path.
- Confirmed: `local()` is called only when the registry read is `undefined` (`serve.ts:6298-6300`); the deferred instance throws the constructor's "Refusing to start in production" error from every call. It is thrown either at the host's `kernel:ready` hook (`serve.ts:6347-6350`) or at the first earlier use; `kernel-base.ts:127-128` dispatches hooks propagating, and `kernel.ts:659-671` rolls back started plugins and rethrows, so the boot stops inside `runtime.start()` exactly as it did when the settings service's `start()` built the eager instance on main. Serve's post-start catch keeps the message-substring branch and adds `HostCryptoProviderRefusal` (`serve.ts:5704`). The message text is unchanged (the test at `:346-359` pins the same `keySource` as `new LocalCryptoProvider()`).
- Timing moved from Phase 2 (settings `start()`) to Phase 3 (`kernel:ready`) for a production boot without a stable key. Between them only other plugins' `start()` run; the HTTP socket opens at `kernel:listening`, after `kernel:ready`, so nothing is served under an unstable key. Noted in ③, not a must-fix.

Two registrations refuse at boot, naming both.
- Confirmed: `refuseTwoCryptoProviderPlugins` (`serve.ts:6368-6387`) is called at `:5650`, before `await runtime.start()` at `:5653`, over the stack-mounted instances (`:4714`, `:4750`) and the resolver-mounted providers, deduplicated by name the way the kernel's own overwrite-by-name works; the refusal names every declaring plugin and the service, never a value. `kernel.use` does not initialize (`kernel.ts:348-355`; Phase 1 is in `bootstrap`), so "before either initializes" holds. An undeclared second `registerService` is refused by the kernel (`kernel.ts:383-386`), naming the service; test `:426-434` pins it. Installed plugins (`registerInstalledPlugins`, `:4767`) are outside the declaration check and inside the kernel's; the PR says so.

No key material in snapshots or logs.
- Confirmed: every refusal string (`serve.ts:6280-6283`, `:6291-6294`, `:6307-6314`, `:6381-6384`) carries the service name, plugin names or missing member names only. The dev diagnostic (`:5695-5697`) prints the service name. The test asserts every refusal against both test keys' hex and base64 (`serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts:79-83`, used at `:415,483,536`). The only snapshot-like assertions are source pins on `serve.ts` text, not values.

The settings shared-instance change (narrowing?).
- Confirmed not a narrowing. On main the default settings service built its own `new LocalCryptoProvider()` in `start()` after `settleKeyFileChannel`; the engine's and binder's instance was the deferred one, built after the same settlement; both read `OS_SECRET_KEY` or the settled key-file channel, i.e. one key. A settings store sealed earlier opens under the shared instance, and the other way round (test `:361-384`, both directions; `:386-400` for a secret field). No reader had a second key to lose. The seat's ruling asked for this to be stated in the PR body; it is, in "No registration".

Tests.
- Confirmed: registered provider seals secret-field writes, datasource credentials and encrypted settings through one instance, and the local fallback is never built (`NO_LOCAL` throws; `:293-333`); the binder, the settings service and the engine hold `host.provider` (`:298,300,310`). No registration: same key source and cross-open (`:336-401`). Two registrations: declared (`:404-416`), one plugin or one composed twice not refused (`:418-424`), undeclared refused by the kernel (`:426-434`). Deferred path (`:437-538`). Source pins on `run()` (`:540-562`).
- Ablation read: replacing `read: () => ctx.getServices().get(CRYPTO_PROVIDER_SERVICE)` with `() => undefined` makes `resolve()` take the local arm; the first test's `local` is `NO_LOCAL`, which throws inside the host's `kernel:ready` hook; `kernel-base.ts:127` propagates it and `kernel.ts:671` rethrows, so `await boot(...)` rejects with "the local fallback was built although a provider is registered" — the red the dev reported. Removing the `refuseTwoCryptoProviderPlugins` call reds `:556-561`; removing the settings `cryptoProvider` handover reds `:549`; a second `setCryptoProvider` or a `new LocalCryptoProvider(` reds `:552-553`. The ablations would go red.
- Confirmed: the file is `integration` tier by `vitest-tiers.ts` (`new ObjectQL(` fires `objectQLCtor`), as the dev says.

Must-fix.
- **M1 — `packages/cli/src/commands/serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts:66` (the `./serve.js` value import) trips main's `Test-source alias gate` (source-reach half).** CI check-run `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` on the head is red at step 45 "Test-source alias gate"; the lane verdict reads "64 gate(s): 63 passed, 1 red … Red: Test-source alias gate". Eight findings, all against this one file: it reaches `import('@objectstack/metadata-protocol')` (serve.ts:3290), `import('@objectstack/metadata')` (serve.ts:3601, 3659), `import('@objectstack/plugin-hono-server')` (serve.ts:3859), `import('@objectstack/rest')` (serve.ts:4884, schema-migration-plugins.ts:1994), `import('@objectstack/driver-turso')` (storage-driver.ts:700, schema-migrate.ts:814), `import('@objectstack/driver-sql')` (schema-migrate.ts:1697, 1703, 1830), `import('@objectstack/platform-objects/plugin')` (schema-migration-plugins.ts:1729, plugin-trust-store.ts:25), `import('@objectstack/plugin-security')` (schema-migration-plugins.ts:1979, 2133) — each a dynamic import inside a function body in the source under test, with no module-scope load in the reach, and each a specifier `@objectstack/cli` resolves through `dist/` (`KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS`). The half judges only test files a change adds or edits, which is why the sibling tests that already import `serve.ts` are not flagged. The gate's own remedy: add module-top side-effect imports to this test file for those eight specifiers (`import '@objectstack/metadata-protocol';` etc.); the source keeps its dynamic imports. Adding `@objectstack/driver-*` value imports does not change the file's tier (already `integration`). Base signature check: `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on the merge-base `1b3e22f0` and on main `000a4c0d`, so this is not a same-signature base red; the half landed on main in acd190b223 (#30969) after the merge-base, and CI runs the merge commit. The fix is in a file inside the claim's surface; the next head owes a delta review of that import block only.

Should-fix.
- S1 — `serve.ts:6342-6345`: `initDone` returns true for any state other than `idle`/`initializing`, so a kernel without `getKernel` (the context type marks it optional) would refuse every seal until the host's own `kernel:ready` hook sets `ready`. Both shipped kernels supply `getKernel` (`kernel.ts:326`, `kernel-base.ts:140`), so this is dormant; a one-line comment naming the assumption is enough.
- S2 — the PR body's "Acceptance notes" list the gaps correctly (one-shot secret commands build their own local provider; installed plugins outside the declaration check; an app-composed `SettingsServicePlugin` not handed the host provider; a declaring plugin that never registers falls back silently). The first is a real gap for a KMS-keyed deployment (`os secret rewrap` cannot open what serve sealed) and should be a card, not a note; the seat carries it (the report names "the seat / cloud#3573" as carrier).

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/cli: patch`, `@objectstack/types: patch`. Right. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an AI author writes changes (no spec key, no stack-config knob, no metadata type), so the level is `patch` on both packages the diff moves. The changeset carries both declaration lines at line start, the widening arm, no BREAKING banner, and states the one no-registration difference (the shared settings instance). It names what a plugin does (`registerService` in `init()`, `providesServices`) and every refusal, with no key value.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Right. The accepted set widens by one published constant (`CRYPTO_PROVIDER_SERVICE` on `@objectstack/types`) and by one host behaviour (`os serve` honours a provider a plugin registered during init). Nothing a consumer could rely on today is taken away: the service name had no reader on main, so no composition registering it could have worked; the new refusals (two declaring plugins, a late or replaced registration, a non-provider value, a seal during init) all sit on paths no shipped consumer uses. Not `(narrowing)`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); no out-of-relay author to name.
- The dev's three deviations, answered: (1) the settings shared instance — accepted above as not a narrowing, stated in the PR body and pinned both ways; (2) `packages/types` in the surface — added by the seat's re-post 6687449788, in claim; (3) `NODE_OPTIONS` heap for the local test-layer typecheck and the unused harness trailer — no code effect.
- `open_questions`: none in the report. `security_findings`: none; this review found none. Key material: none printed anywhere.
- Timing note, not a flag: a production boot without a stable key now refuses at `kernel:ready` (Phase 3) instead of at the settings service's `start()` (Phase 2); same message, same `runtime.start()` rejection, socket not yet open. The PR body says "still fires at `kernel:ready`", which is accurate.
- Narrowing check on the init-time refusal: a seal or open through the binder during plugin init now refuses where main would have built the local provider; no shipped consumer does this, and doing it would have read the key file before the boot chose it. Not a narrowing of a declared capability.
- Out-of-scope findings the dev named (one-shot secret commands; installed plugins outside the declaration check; app-composed settings plugin; declare-but-never-register) are read and agreed; the first should become a card (S2).
- The head is red on one gate (M1). Any auto-merge on this head would be disarmed by rule; none is armed (draft PR).

### Check-runs on the head (read at 16:17Z, API)

60 check-runs: 23 success, 9 skipped, 2 failure, 26 in_progress. Red: `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (job 127999666346, step 68 "Lane verdict" after step 45 "Test-source alias gate" failed under continue-on-error) and its aggregator `Lint & Repo Gates`. Signature: step "Test-source alias gate", first error line "✗ packages/cli/src/commands/serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts:66: reaches `import('@objectstack/metadata-protocol')` in the source under test, at packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:3290". Merge-base `1b3e22f0` and main `000a4c0d` are green on `Lint & Repo Gates`, so the red is the PR's own. Test Core, Test UI, Type Check · workspace and Type Check UI were still running at the read.

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `fbc8206285c9f7877adbe479cd7bb525a603efd3`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs --changed-from origin/main` run once on a detached worktree of the head (no install, no build; the script needs only sibling scripts and node builtins) to answer whether the eight module-top imports clear main's source-reach half; run a second time on the pre-fix merge commit `816331a1` to show the same probe reds there with exactly the eight specifiers, so its green on the head is a reading, not a run that judged nothing. Delta over record 6689701608 (head `2ff85dad…`). The new head is two commits on the old one: `816331a1`, a merge of `origin/main` at `c77dd17f` (which carries the source-reach half of the gate, acd190b223), and `fbc82062`, the fix. Nothing else moved; the PR's file list is the same five paths (+933/−60 against main). This record judges only the two commits; everything the full record confirmed about the provider selection, the three consumers, the refusals and the changeset stands unchanged, because the fix commit touches no code.

- Merge `816331a1`: `git merge-tree --write-tree 2ff85dad c77dd17f` yields tree `e9eeb06b…`, byte-identical to the merge commit's tree. No conflict, no hand edit. `git diff c77dd17f 816331a1` is exactly the PR's five files.
